words.gloss: powder (cūrṇa) of: kuṣṭha (costus, Saussurea costus, standard); elā (small cardamom, Elettaria cardamomum, standard); lāṅgalī (glory lily, Gloriosa superba, standard); vacā (sweet flag, Acorus calamus, standard); cyanya (unclear); citraka (leadwort, Plumbago zeylanica, standard); cirabilva (probably Indian elm, Holoptelea integrifolia, probable)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, तब इसे कुष्ठ यानी कूठ, एला यानी छोटी इलायची, लाङ्गली यानी कलिहारी, वचा यानी बच, च्यन्य नाम का अस्पष्ट शब्द, चित्रक यानी चीता और चिरबिल्व यानी सम्भवतः चिलबिल का चूर्ण बार-बार सूँघने के लिए देना चाहिए।
english: On a conjectural reading: then one should give her, to smell again and again, a powder of kuṣṭha (costus), elā (small cardamom), lāṅgalī (glory lily), vacā (sweet flag), cyanya (unclear), citraka (leadwort) and cirabilva (probably the Indian elm).

text_flags.why: possible: 'cyanya' is not a drug name; cavya (Piper chaba, long-pepper relative) is often paired with citraka and vacā in such lists, and 'cavya' could be misread as 'cyanya'. Not certain, so the word is kept unclear.
possible: 'upāghātum' is not a valid infinitive; 'upāghrātum' (to smell) fits a powder given 'muhurmuhuḥ' (again and again)

notes: Print habit for the whole chunk: anusvāra is written for homorganic nasals (lāṃgalī, jṛṃbhaṇa, maṃdira), and doubled -rtt- (parivarttate) and ṣṭh/ṣṭ and muśala/musala spellings vary; `words` give the standard forms and none of these is flagged again. The compound is a drug list; its fifth member 'cyanya' is unclear in print (kept unsplit, translated as unclear), so the list is read on a conjectural reading. 'upāghātuṃ' is read as upāghrātum (to smell), also conjectural. Verb 'dadyāt' has no stated subject (one/she who attends). Identification tags: kuṣṭha, elā, lāṅgalī, vacā, citraka standard; cirabilva probable. Hindi names: कुष्ठ=कूठ, एला=छोटी इलायची, लाङ्गली=कलिहारी, वचा=बच, चित्रक=चीता, चिरबिल्व=चिलबिल (probable).

words.gloss: birch (bhūrja, Betula utilis, standard); bark (patra); śiśipā (sissoo / Indian rosewood, Dalbergia sissoo, standard); sarja (sāl tree, Shorea robusta, standard)

hindi: वैसे ही भूर्जपत्र यानी भोजपत्र, शिंशपा यानी शीशम, या सर्ज यानी साल के रस, इनमें से किसी एक का धूम यानी धुआँ, बीच-बीच में भी।
english: Likewise, the smoke of any one of birch bark (bhūrjapatra), śiśipā (sissoo) or the sap (rasa) of sarja (sāl), and at intervals.
notes: Elliptical: the verb (dadyāt, 'one should give') is carried from the previous units, so the line is translated without a verb. 'sarja' (end of token 2) and 'rasa' (start of token 3) are read together as sarja-rasa, 'sap of sarja'; the print separates them, and 'rasa' could alternatively be a separate item. The whole is one compound: [bhūrjapatra, śiśipā, sarjarasa]-anyatama-dhūma. 'antarāntarā ca' is read as 'and at intervals' (between the sniffings). Tags: bhūrja, śiśipā, sarja standard; the resin sense of rasa is the usual one but is an interpretation.

words.gloss: regions of: side (pārśva); back (pṛṣṭha); waist/hip (kaṭī); thigh (sakthi)

hindi: उसके पार्श्व, पीठ, कटि और जाँघ के प्रदेशों का गुनगुने तेल से अभ्यंग करके सुखपूर्वक मर्दन करे।
english: Having anointed the regions of her sides, back, waist and thighs with lukewarm oil, one should knead them comfortably.

text_flags.why: possible: 'mṛdgīyāt' is not a form; the optative of mṛd (9th class) is mṛdnīyāt, and sense fits (rubbing after anointing); n/g confusion is common in this print

notes: 'asyā' stands for asyāḥ with the visarga dropped before the voiced m of the next word; this is regular sandhi, not a typo. 'deśa' = region/part. 'tailena' is oil unspecified. The same sandhi applies in units 58, 61, 78 and 82.

hindi: इस प्रकार गर्भ नीचे की ओर पलट जाता है।
english: Thus the fetus (garbha) turns around, downward.
notes: 'avāk' is taken as the adverb 'downward'; the line does not say which part of the fetus leads, and no position is stated. 'evam' refers to the preceding procedure (units 47-49).

hindi: उसका लक्षण।
english: Its sign (lakṣaṇa).
notes: GROUPING: this short unit appears to introduce unit 52, which then states the sign. 'tasya' most likely refers to the turning of the fetus in 50. Copula understood.

hindi: हृदय को छोड़कर वह उदर यानी पेट में प्रवेश करता है और बस्ति यानी सम्भवतः मूत्राशय के सिर को पकड़ लेता है।
english: Having left the heart (hṛdaya), it enters the belly (udara) and takes hold of the head of the bladder (basti, probably).
notes: Subject (the fetus, from 50) is not stated here. 'basti' is the bladder in this anatomical context (tag probable); 'śiras' = head/top. 'avagṛṇhāti' is an attested spelling variant of avagṛhṇāti. The sign is that the fetus leaves the region of the heart and descends; the text says nothing more.

words.gloss: she is to be made to do

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, वे उसे जल्दी करने को प्रेरित करते हैं, आढ्यः अस्पष्ट शब्द है। यदि वह इस प्रकार नहीं पलटता, तब उससे बार-बार जम्हाई लेना और टहलना कराना चाहिए, और अभी पहले कही गई विधि भी।
english: On a conjectural reading: they urge her on, āḍhyaḥ (unclear). If it does not turn in this way, then she should be made to do yawning and walking about again and again, and the procedure stated just before.

text_flags.why: possible: 'āḍhyaḥ' (nom. sg. 'rich, abounding') makes no sense after 'tvarayanti enām'; probably a corrupt word for a plural subject (for example something like 'pains'); not resolvable from the print, so it is left unsplit and unclear
possible: stray anusvāra in 'anantaroṃktam'; the sense 'anantara-uktam' (stated just before) fits

notes: 'āḍhyaḥ' is damaged or corrupt, so 'tvarayanti enām' (they hasten her) is translated only on a conjectural reading and without a firm subject. 'kārayitavyā' agrees with an understood 'strī' (the woman, nominative); the three accusatives (yawning, walking about, the procedure) are what she is to be made to do. 'The procedure stated just before' appears to point back to units 47-49. 'parivarttate' (doubled -rtt-) is normalised to parivartate.

hindi: दूसरे तो कहते हैं कि अनाज से भरी ओखली पर मूसल से प्रहार करना चाहिए।
english: Others, however, say that a mortar filled with grain is to be struck with a pestle.
notes: 'muśala' is a variant spelling of musala (pestle). 'dhānya' is grain, kind not stated. The purpose is not stated in this unit; the next unit rejects this view. The closing 'iti' marks the report of the others' opinion.

hindi: वह तो ठीक नहीं है।
english: That, however, is not right.

text_flags.why: possible: long ū in 'tū' is not needed; 'tat tu' (that, however) is meant

notes: Copula understood. 'tat' refers to the view reported in 54.

hindi: गर्भिणी के लिए कठोर व्यायाम से बचना सदा बताया जाता है।
english: For the avoidance of severe exertion is constantly prescribed for a pregnant woman.
notes: 'garbhiṇyāḥ' (genitive) is rendered 'for a pregnant woman' (genitive of the person concerned). 'vyāyāma' = exertion.

words.gloss: of her in whom all (sarva) dhātus and doṣas are set in motion (pracalita)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, और विशेषकर प्रसव के समय, जिसके सब धातु और दोष चलायमान हो गए हैं उसके, कोमलता के कारण, त्रार्या अस्पष्ट शब्द है, मुशल्यायाम अस्पष्ट शब्द है जिसका अनुमानित अर्थ मूसल का श्रम है, उससे प्रेरित वायु अवसर पाकर प्राणों को हानि पहुँचा सकती है।
english: On a conjectural reading: and especially at the time of delivery, in her whose dhātus and doṣas have all been set in motion, because of delicacy (trāryā, unclear), the wind (vāyu), stirred up by muśalyāyāma (unclear; conjecturally exertion with a pestle), having found an opening, might injure the vital breaths (prāṇa).

text_flags.why: possible: 'trāryā' is not a word; it may be a corrupt 'nāryāḥ' (of the woman) but this is not certain, so it is kept unclear
possible: 'muśalyāyāma' is not a word; context (units 54-56: pestle, severe exertion) suggests muśala-vyāyāma or muśala-āyāma, 'exertion with a pestle'; not certain
possible: vāyuḥ + antaram should join as 'vāyur antaram'; the r is missing in print

notes: Two damaged words, 'trāryā' and 'muśalyāyāma', are kept unsplit and marked unclear; the sentence is therefore a conjectural reading. 'dhātu-doṣa' in the bahuvrīhi is taken as dvandva 'dhātus and doṣas'. 'antara' = opening/gap (alternative: opportunity). The closing 'iti' gives the reason for the prohibition in 56. 'hiṃsyāt' is a statement of what might happen, not a certain result.

hindi: तब कुशल स्त्री, गर्भ के पलट जाने पर उस स्त्री को पलंग पर बिठाकर, बैठी हुई उसके पैरों की ओर से योनि यानी जननमार्ग का अनुलोम दिशा में सुखपूर्वक अभ्यंग करके, दोनों नितम्बों को पैरों से दबाए।
english: Then a skilled woman, having placed her whose fetus has turned on a couch (paryaṅka), and, from the foot-side of her as she sits, having anointed the yoni (vagina) comfortably in the natural direction (anuloma), should press the two buttocks (sphij) with the two feet.
notes: 'pādābhyām' ('with the two feet') does not say whose feet; the natural reading is the attendant's. 'paryaṅka' = couch (alternative: a seated posture). 'anuloma' = in the natural direction (with the grain / downward); the text gives no further detail. The substance anointed is not named. 'niṣaṇṇāyā' = niṣaṇṇāyāḥ with regular visarga loss before y.

hindi: और योनि को बार-बार फैलाए।
english: And she should stretch out the yoni (vagina) again and again.
notes: Subject (the skilled woman of 58) is not stated here. The text does not say how the yoni is stretched.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, और कहे: हे सौभाग्यवती, धीरे-धीरे प्रवाहण करो यानी नीचे की ओर बल लगाओ, तुम्हारे मुख का वर्ण बहुत निर्मल है, तुम पुत्र को जन्म दोगी।
english: On a conjectural reading: and she should say, "O fortunate one, bear down (pravāhaṇa) gently, gently; the colour of your face is very clear; you will bear a son."

text_flags.why: possible: 'suprasanna' + 'ete' makes no sense with 'te mukhavarṇaḥ'; the nominative 'suprasannaḥ te' (your ... very clear) fits
possible: the addressee is 'you', so the 2nd person 'janayiṣyasi' is expected; the printed 3rd person 'janayiṣyati' has no stated subject

notes: Two small corrections (above) are adopted in `words` and marked in the translation. As printed, 'janayiṣyati' would have the face-colour or an unstated 'she' as subject. 'pravāhaṇa' = pushing/bearing down; the speaker (the attendant) addresses the woman in labour. The closing 'iti' ends the quoted speech.

hindi: दूसरी तो इसके बाएँ कान में यह मन्त्र जपे।
english: Another (woman), however, should mutter this mantra in her left ear.
notes: 'anyā' is feminine, so another woman is meant; the noun is not stated. The mantra follows in 62 onward.

hindi: पृथ्वी, जल, आकाश, तेज यानी अग्नि, वायु, विष्णु, प्रजापति।
english: Earth, water, sky (viyat), fire (tejas), wind, Viṣṇu, Prajāpati.
notes: GROUPING: this list of names (the mantra) has no verb; it appears to continue in unit 63, whose verbs (pātu, dadhātu) probably have these as subjects. The verbs in 63 are singular although seven names are listed.

hindi: गर्भ सहित तुम्हारी सदा रक्षा करे, या शल्य से मुक्ति भी प्रदान करे।
english: May (it) always protect you, together with the fetus, or also grant freedom from the dart (śalya).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 62. Subject is not stated in this unit; the verbs are singular, probably agreeing with the list in 62 taken together. 'śalya' = dart (also a foreign body or a piercing pain); its precise sense here is not certain, so it is not interpreted. 'vaiśalya' = state without the dart. The sense of 'vā ... api' ('or ... also') is loose.

words.gram: ppp. a-vi-√kliś, m. acc. sg. or adv.

hindi: हे सुन्दर मुख वाली, तुम अपीड़ित रहकर अपीड़ित को जन्म दो।
english: Give birth, you who are unharmed, to the unharmed (one), O fair-faced one.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue in 65, where 'putram' (son) is the object, so the first 'avikliṣṭam' most likely agrees with it; it could instead be the adverb 'without distress'. The printed letter ḻ (in avikḻiṣṭa) is normalised to l, a print habit recorded once for this book.

hindi: कार्तिकेय की कान्ति वाले, कार्तिकेय से रक्षित पुत्र को।
english: A son having the splendour of Kārtikeya, protected by Kārtikeya.
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'prasūṣva' (give birth) is carried from 64, so no verb is supplied. Kārtikeya is the name of a god, as printed. The closing 'iti' ends the mantra.

hindi: तथा।
english: Likewise.
notes: Connecting word before a second mantra (67 onward).

words.gloss: Citrabhānu (bright-rayed; an epithet of fire or sun)

hindi: यहाँ अमृत और सोम और चित्रभानु, हे भामिनी।
english: Here: nectar (amṛta), and Soma, and Citrabhānu, O lady.
notes: GROUPING: no verb here; the plural verb 'nivasantu' in 68 appears to complete this line. 'citrabhānu' is an epithet (of fire or the sun); which is meant is not stated, so only the epithet is given.

words.gloss: in the house, in the abode

hindi: और उच्चैःश्रवा घोड़ा तुम्हारे घर में निवास करें।
english: And Uccaiḥśravas, the horse: may (they) dwell in your house.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 67; the plural verb probably has amṛta, Soma, Citrabhānu and Uccaiḥśravas as subjects. 'te' is taken as 'your' (alternatively 'to you'). 'mandira' is house/dwelling.

hindi: जलों से निकाला गया यह अमृत निश्चय ही, हे स्त्री, तुम्हारे इस गर्भ को शीघ्र छोड़ दे।
english: This nectar (amṛta), indeed drawn up from the waters: may it quickly release this fetus of yours, O woman.
notes: 'stri' is the regular vocative of strī. 'laghu' is taken as the adverb 'quickly' (alternative: lightly, easily).

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, इसलिए अग्नि, वायु, सूर्य और इन्द्र, लवण जल धारण करने वालों के साथ, तुम्हें शान्ति दें।
english: On a conjectural reading: therefore may fire (anala), wind (pavana), sun (arka) and Indra (Vāsava), together with the bearers of salt water, grant you peace (śānti).

text_flags.why: possible: 'analpavana' (a-l-p-a-v) is not a word; anala-pavana (fire, wind) fits the list with arka and Vāsava, and the a/p letters look swapped

notes: The list reading depends on the correction above. 'te' is taken as the enclitic 'to you' (alternative: 'they'). 'lavaṇāmbudhara' is literally 'bearer(s) of salt water'; whether oceans or clouds is not clear, so it is left literal. 'arka' = sun here (arka is also a plant name). 'tat' = therefore (alternative: that).

hindi: वैसे ही दूसरी समझाए।
english: Likewise another (woman) should instruct (her).
notes: 'parā' is feminine, so a woman is meant. The object (the woman in labour) is not stated; the instruction appears to follow in 72-76.

hindi: वेदना के न आने पर प्रवाहण मत करो।
english: When the pain (vedanā) has not come, do not bear down.

text_flags.why: possible: 'praivāhiṭṭāḥ' is not a form; mā + the aorist 'pravāhiṣṭhāḥ' (do not bear down) fits, and unit 75 has the same verb as 'prabāhiṣṭāḥ'

notes: The aorist form of pra-√vah (instead of the causative used in 60, pravāhayasva) is as printed in both 72 and 75; the grammar is not fully certain, but the sense is clear from 73.

words.gloss: bearing down at the wrong time
of the urges (vega) of feces, urine and the rest
because of causing: breathlessness (śvāsa, standard); cough (kāsa, standard); wasting (śoṣa, probable); hunchedness (kubjatā); and so on

hindi: असमय प्रवाहण मल, मूत्र आदि के वेगों को जबरन निकालने के समान है, निरर्थक है और गर्भ के लिए अहितकर है, क्योंकि वह श्वास यानी साँस फूलना, कास यानी खाँसी, शोष यानी सूखकर घटते जाना, कुब्जता यानी कूबड़ापन आदि करता है।
english: For bearing down at the wrong time (akāla-pravāhaṇa) is like forcing out the urges (vega) of feces, urine and the rest; it is useless and unwholesome for the fetus, because it causes breathlessness (śvāsa), cough (kāsa), wasting (śoṣa), hunchedness (kubjatā) and so on.
notes: Copula understood. 'garbhasya' is taken with 'ahitam' (unwholesome for the fetus); it could also go with the list of harms. The harms are stated by the text as consequences of untimely bearing down. 'śoṣa' = wasting (in older usage sometimes consumption); kept as 'wasting'.

hindi: वैसे ही वेदना में प्रवाहण न करना उन्हीं के रोकने के समान है, हानि के लिए होता है।
english: Likewise, not bearing down when there is pain (vedanā) is like the holding back of those very (urges), and leads to injury.
notes: 'teṣām' refers back to the urges (vega) in 73. Copula understood; 'upaghātāya' (dative of purpose) is rendered 'leads to injury'. The text does not say what injury.

hindi: तब जैसा कहा गया है वैसा करो, धीरे-धीरे, और पहले प्रवाहण करो।
english: Then do as stated, gently, gently, and at first bear down.

text_flags.why: possible: b/v confusion and lost -h-; same verb as in unit 72 (pravāhiṣṭhāḥ)

notes: GROUPING: 75 and 76 appear to form one sentence about the stages of bearing down. 'pūrvam' = first/at first.

words.gloss: on arrival at the mouth of the yoni

hindi: गर्भ के निकलने पर जोर से, योनि के मुख तक पहुँचने पर और अधिक जोर से, प्रसव तक।
english: Strongly at the exit of the fetus; more strongly on arrival at the mouth of the yoni, until delivery.
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'pravāhiṣṭhāḥ' (bear down) is carried from 75, so none is supplied. 'garbhasya' probably governs both 'nirgame' and 'pratipattau'. The closing 'iti' ends the instruction.

words.gram: pres. part. mid. pra-√vah, f. gen. sg.

hindi: उस प्रवाहण करती हुई स्त्री के लिए वे यह शब्द करें: जन्म दे दिया, जन्म दे दिया, धन्य, धन्य पुत्र को!
english: For that woman who is bearing down, they should raise a cry: "She has given birth, she has given birth, to a blessed, blessed son!"
notes: The genitives 'tasyāḥ ... striyāḥ' are taken as 'for/over that woman'; the exact relation is loose. The subject of 'kuryuḥ' (they) is not stated. 'prajātā' is used actively ('has given birth'). 'dhanya' = blessed (alternatively fortunate).

hindi: इस प्रकार उसके प्राण हर्ष से पुष्ट होते हैं।
english: Thus her vital breaths (prāṇa) are nourished by joy.
notes: 'āpyāyyante' = are nourished/refreshed/swollen; rendered 'nourished'. The cry of 77 is the evident cause of the joy.

words.gloss: in retention (obstruction) of the fetus; garbha-saṅga, probably obstructed labour (probable)
with the sloughed skin of a black snake
with piṇḍītaka (probably emetic nut, Randia dumetorum, probable)

hindi: गर्भसंग यानी गर्भ के रुकने में, योनि यानी जननमार्ग को काले साँप की केंचुली से या पिण्डीतक यानी सम्भवतः मैनफल से धूपित करे।
english: In garbha-saṅga (retention of the fetus; probably obstructed labour), one should fumigate the yoni (vagina) with the sloughed skin of a black snake, or with piṇḍītaka (probably the emetic nut).
notes: 'saṅga' = sticking/obstruction; the modern equivalent 'obstructed labour' is a probable reading, not stated. 'kṛṣṇasarpa' is literally 'black snake'; the species is not stated. 'nirmokena' is printed with n for ṇ (orthographic). piṇḍītaka is commonly equated with madana (Randia dumetorum) but the identity is not certain.

hindi: और हिरण्यपुष्पी की जड़, जिसकी पहचान अज्ञात है, हाथ और पैर में बाँधे।
english: And one should tie the root of hiraṇyapuṣpī (unidentified) on the hand and foot.
notes: 'hiraṇyapuṣpī' (literally 'golden-flowered') is not identified here: sources differ and no safe identification is given. 'hastapāde' is a singular collective 'hand and foot'; the text does not say whose or whether both sides.

hindi: और सुवर्चला, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, या विशल्या, जो सम्भवतः लाङ्गली यानी कलिहारी है, धारण करे।
english: And one should hold suvarcalā (identity disputed) or viśalyā (probably the same as lāṅgalī).
notes: GROUPING: 80 and 81 appear to continue one another (things to tie or hold). suvarcalā is disputed (candidates include Cleome gynandra and others); viśalyā is a recognised synonym of lāṅgalī (Gloriosa superba) in the drug lists, tagged probable.

hindi: अब यदि प्रसव कर चुकी स्त्री का अपरा यानी जेर नहीं गिरता, तब दाहिने हाथ से नाभि के ऊपर से जोर से दबाकर और पीछे की ओर से पकड़कर हिलाए।
english: Now, if the placenta (aparā) of one who has delivered does not fall out, then, pressing firmly with the right hand from above the navel and gripping from behind, one should shake.
notes: 'prasūtāyā na' is regular sandhi for prasūtāyāḥ na. The object of 'upasaṅgṛhya' and 'vidhūnuyāt' is not stated (not even the abdomen), so none is supplied; 'upariṣṭhāt' is printed with ṣṭh (variant of upariṣṭāt). 'aparā' = placenta/afterbirth (standard).

hindi: या एड़ी से श्रोणि यानी कूल्हे पर प्रहार करे।
english: Or one should strike the hip (śroṇi) with the heel.

text_flags.why: possible: instrumental 'pāṣṇyā' (with the heel) is expected; the anusvāra looks like a stray mark (a locative would be 'pāṣṇyām', 'on the heel')

notes: 'śroṇi' = hip/pelvic region (alternative: buttock). The text does not say whose heel.

hindi: या दोनों नितम्बों को पकड़कर खूब दबाए।
english: Or, having gripped the two buttocks (sphij), one should press them thoroughly.
notes: 'supīḍitam pīḍayet' is a cognate expression, 'press so that it is well pressed'.

hindi: वेणी से, या बालों से लिपटी अँगुली से, कण्ठ और तालु को स्पर्श करे।
english: With a braid, or with a finger wound round with hair, one should touch the throat (kaṇṭha) and palate (tālu).
notes: 'keśaveṣṭitayā' is taken with 'aṅgulyā' (the finger wound with hair); it could also go with 'veṇyā'. The text states no effect of the touch.

words.gloss: with birch bark (bhūrjapatra); kāca-maṇi (literally 'glass-gem', sense doubtful); snake slough
with bhūrja (birch) and guggulu (Indian bdellium, Commiphora wightii, standard)

hindi: और भूर्जपत्र यानी भोजपत्र, काचमणि जिसका अर्थ यहाँ संदिग्ध है, और साँप की केंचुली से योनि यानी जननमार्ग को धूपित करे, या भूर्ज और गुग्गुल से।
english: And one should fumigate the yoni (vagina) with birch bark (bhūrjapatra), kāca-maṇi (literally 'glass-gem'; sense doubtful) and snake slough, or with bhūrja and guggulu (Indian bdellium).
notes: 'kāca-maṇi' is taken literally (glass + gem/bead); fumigating with glass is odd, so the word may be corrupt (for example a plant name); not resolved and not interpreted. The print joins 'dhūpayet' to 'bhūrja' (no space). 'nirmoka' = slough.

words.gloss: cooked with the root of śāli (a rice variety, Oryza sativa)
with bitter bottle gourd (kaṭukālābu, Lagenaria siceraria, probable); jālinī (a Luffa, disputed); nimba (neem, Azadirachta indica, standard); snake slough

hindi: या शालि की जड़ के साथ पकाए घी से योनि का अभ्यंग करके सम्भवतः कड़वी लौकी, जालिनी यानी सम्भवतः तोरई जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, निम्ब यानी नीम और साँप की केंचुली से धूपन करे।
english: Or, having anointed the yoni (vagina) with ghee cooked with śāli root, one should fumigate with probably bitter bottle gourd (kaṭukālābu), jālinī (a Luffa; disputed), nimba (neem) and snake slough.

text_flags.why: possible: the a of abhyajya is lost in print
possible: ḍ for ṭ in 'kaduka'; 'alāmbu' is a valid variant of alābu and is not changed

notes: 'kaṭukālābu' is read as one drug, 'bitter bottle gourd'; the alternative is two drugs, kaṭukā (probably Picrorhiza kurroa) and alābu. 'śāli' is a rice variety; 'śālimūla' could in principle be a shortened name of another plant, so only the literal sense is given. 'siddha' = cooked. 'jālinī' is disputed (Luffa species are the usual guess).

words.gloss: mixed with kaṭu oil (pungent oil, probably mustard oil, probable)

hindi: या जिसका अभ्यंग न हुआ हो उसे, कटुतैल यानी सम्भवतः सरसों के तेल से मिले हुए, कल्क बनाए हुए, या तेल से लिपे हुए से लेप करे।
english: Or, for one not anointed, one should smear with (ones) mixed with kaṭu oil (probably mustard oil) and made into a paste (kalka), or smeared with oil.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 87. The nouns are not stated: 'anabhyaktām' (feminine, probably the yoni or the woman) and the three instrumentals (probably the fumigants of 87, but not stated) are left as in the Sanskrit. The structure of the two 'vā' is uncertain. 'kaṭu-taila' (pungent oil) is probably mustard oil, a modern reading.

words.gloss: with a paste (kalka) of jaggery (guḍa) and dry ginger (nāgara, Zingiber officinale, standard)

hindi: या गुड़ और नागर यानी सोंठ के कल्क से।
english: Or with a paste (kalka) of jaggery (guḍa) and dry ginger (nāgara).
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'ālimpet' (should smear) is carried from 88, so none is supplied. The next unit says that this very paste may be eaten.

hindi: या उसी को खाए।
english: Or she should eat that very (paste).
notes: 'tat' most probably refers to the guḍa-nāgara paste of 89; the noun is not stated. Subject is the woman (not stated).

words.gloss: with a paste (kalka) of lāṅgalī root

hindi: या लाङ्गली की जड़ के कल्क से हाथ और पेट पर लेप करे।
english: Or with a paste (kalka) of lāṅgalī root one should smear the hand and the belly (udara).

text_flags.why: possible: short u in 'mula'; 'mūla' (root) is the expected word

notes: 'pāṇim' is singular ('hand'); the text does not say whether one or both hands. lāṅgalī: see unit 47.

words.gloss: milk (sap) of mahāvṛkṣa (disputed, probably a spurge such as snuhī)

hindi: या महावृक्ष, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, सम्भवतः थूहर, का दूध सिर पर डाले।
english: Or one should pour the milk (kṣīra) of mahāvṛkṣa (disputed; probably a spurge such as snuhī) over the head.
notes: 'mahāvṛkṣa' (literally 'great tree') is a drug name whose identity varies by source; tagged disputed. 'kṣīra' of a plant = milky sap (latex).
